extracted.intended_audience: public relations practitioners, corporate leaders, journalists, and students of public relations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for the practice of public relations counsel: how to study and gauge public opinion, choose media and instruments, advise clients on policy and presentation, and act as a constructive intermediary between organizations and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be a student of the public mind
rubrics_metrics.description: The public relations counsel is first of all a student. His field of study is the public mind. His text books for this study are the facts of life; the articles printed in newspapers and magazines, the advertisements ... the sermons issuing from pulpits, anecdotes ... the gossip of Wall Street, the patter of the theater and the conversation of other men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constantly observe varied sources (news, ads, billboards, speeches, gossip, theater conversation) to understand the state of public opinion; treat public opinion as a subject for systematic study rather than intuition alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop sensitiveness to the state of mind of the public
rubrics_metrics.description: Now sensitiveness to the state of mind of the public is a difficult thing to achieve or maintain. Any man can tell you his own reactions; few have the time, interest or training to develop a sense of what other persons think or feel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate specialized ability akin to a clinical sense through painstaking self-criticism and experience; value newspaper or similar training that sharpens 'the needle' sensing public likes and dislikes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ research campaigns, symposiums and surveys
rubrics_metrics.description: Of course, the public relations counsel employs all those practical means of gauging the public mind which modern advertising has developed and uses. He employs the research campaign, the symposium, the survey of a particular group or of a particular state of mind as a further aid, and confirmation or modification of his own appraisals and judgments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use formal research methods (surveys, symposiums, campaigns) to confirm or revise intuitive appraisals; treat research as an integral check on judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a wide range of instruments and media
rubrics_metrics.description: There are the instruments by which he broadcasts facts and ideas to the public; advertising, motion pictures, circular letters, booklets, handbills, speeches, meetings, parades, news articles, magazine articles and whatever other mediums there are through which public attention is reached and influenced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select and combine media (press, radio, lecture platform, advertising, stage, motion picture, mails, events) appropriate to audience and message rather than relying on a single channel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advise on actions as well as communications
rubrics_metrics.description: He is becoming to-day as much of an adviser on actions as he is the communicator of these actions to the public. His primary function now is ... to advise his clients how positive results can be accomplished in the field of public relations and to keep them from drifting inadvertently into unfortunate or harmful situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counsel should recommend policy or operational changes (not only messaging) when necessary to align client behavior with public expectations and avoid reputational harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret the public to the client and the client to the public
rubrics_metrics.description: The public relations counsel is the pleader to the public of a point of view. He acts in this capacity as a consultant both in interpreting the public to his client and in helping to interpret his client to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform two-way translation: advise clients on public sentiment and tailor public-facing explanations that make the client's position intelligible and acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be proactive rather than merely a 'publicity man'
rubrics_metrics.description: The public relations counsel's primary function now is not to bring his clients by chance to the public’s attention ... but to advise his clients how positive results can be accomplished ... The very fact that many of the largest corporations ... are recognizing the need of maintaining right relationships with the public is alone important enough to assure a fair and even favorable hearing for their public relations departments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid opportunistic or stunt-based publicity; pursue sustained programs that build long-term understanding and relationships with the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish counsel from press agent/publicity man
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a familiar tinge to them ... but in justice to the men who bear these titles ... it should be said that they are—or can be—dissociated from the old idea of 'publicity man.' ... a man who merely represents the old idea of getting something for nothing from publishers is about passé.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uphold professional standards beyond 'getting something for nothing'; aim for constructive, ethical practice rather than manipulation or bribery of the press.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be alive to day-by-day events and informal communications
rubrics_metrics.description: The public relations counsel must be alive to the events of the day—not only the events that are printed but the events which are forming hour by hour, as reported in the words that are spoken on the street, in the smoking cars, in the school room, or expressed in any of the other forms of thought communication that make up public opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor informal, local, and evolving conversations as well as formal media; maintain real-time awareness to adapt counsel quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider broader social and labor conditions in messaging
rubrics_metrics.description: He may to-day consider, for instance, in his sales campaign, not only the quality of his soap but the working conditions, the hours of labor, even the living conditions of the men who make it. The public relations counsel must advise him on these factors as well as on their presentation to the public most interested in them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate client practices (labor, environment, community relations) into PR strategy; address underlying issues, not only product features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build cooperative public-spirited programs to foster favorable opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: This department studies the public and tries to discover where the railroad’s service can be mended or improved... It coöperates, for example, with such movements as the Welcome Stranger Committee of New York City in distributing literature to travelers ... It coöperates with conventions, to the extent of arranging special travel facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage in cooperative civic or service initiatives (assistance at conventions, traveler aids, community programs) to create demonstrable public benefit and goodwill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain continuous 'selling' even for non-competitive services
rubrics_metrics.description: Even a service which is in a large measure non-competitive must continually 'sell' itself to the public, as evidenced by the strenuous efforts of the New York subways and elevated lines to keep themselves constantly before the people in the most favorable possible aspect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep ongoing communications and reputation management for all services, emphasizing constructive framing to mitigate inevitable inconveniences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide informative and accurate publicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Among the improvements ... which Mr. Hoover anticipates from widespread, accurate and informative publicity about the industry itself, are the stimulation of industrial consumers ... the ability of the consumer to 'form some judgment as to the prices he should pay for coal,' and the tendency to hold down over-expansion in the industry by publication of the ratio of production to capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design publicity to be factual and informative; accurate information can improve consumer behavior, industry forecasting, and public trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study and correct public impressions for public-utility type organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Some public utilities maintain public relations departments, whose function it is to interpret the organizations to the public, as much as to interpret the public to them. The significant thing ... is that public opinion is becoming cumulatively more and more articulate and therefore more important to industrial life as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For organizations with public-interest charge, actively research public perceptions, identify misconceptions, and correct them through transparent communication and service improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use public education campaigns for health and civic problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Publicity is, in fact, one of the major functions of the Health Department, inasmuch as its constructive work depends to a considerable extent upon the public education it provides in combating evils and in building up a spirit of individual and group coöperation in all health matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ PR as a tool for public education (health, safety, prevention) to produce behavioral and cooperative outcomes beneficial to the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the character and origins of public opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: The character and origins of public opinion, the factors that make up the individual mind and the group mind must be understood if the profession of public relations counsel is to be intelligently practiced ... Public opinion is the aggregate result of individual opinions—now uniform, now conflicting—of the men and women who make up society or any group of society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze how individual beliefs (often dogmatic and authority-based) aggregate into group opinion; tailor strategies recognizing that public opinion is uneven, changeable, and rooted in varied authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize dogmatism, intolerance, and 'logic-proof compartments' in audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: It is axiomatic that men who know little are often intolerant of a point of view that is contrary to their own... We find here with significant uniformity what one psychologist has called 'logic-proof compartments.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate resistance based on entrenched beliefs; design communications that avoid direct confrontation with identity-defining convictions and instead use indirect persuasion, education, or trusted authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise discretion rather than leave matters to reporters
rubrics_metrics.description: The enormous discretion as to what facts and what impressions shall be reported is steadily convincing every organized group of people that, whether it wishes to secure publicity or to avoid it, the exercise of discretion cannot be left to the reporter. It is safer to hire a press agent who stands between the group and the newspapers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manage information flow proactively; control framing by preparing spokespeople, releases and intermediaries rather than expecting unbiased reporter selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value relevant professional background (e.g., newspaper training)
rubrics_metrics.description: Charles J. Rosebault ... remarks that the competent public relations counsel has generally had some newspaper training and that the value of this training 'is a keen sense of the likes and dislikes of what we call the public.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek or value experience in journalism, advertising, or related fields that build practical sensing of public preferences and effective media relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim to be a constructive community force and accelerate interest in matters of value
rubrics_metrics.description: The public relations consultant is ideally a constructive force in the community. The results of his work are often accelerated interest in matters of value and importance to the social, economic or political life of the community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure success not only by client advantage but by positive civic outcomes—stimulating public interest in socially valuable issues and fostering cooperation.
